answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, a full primary switch would meet the 18% target on price but introduces avoidable delivery risk. The stronger move is to use the low-cost quote as a benchmark to renegotiate incumbent price/payment/volume terms before expiry, preserving continuity while pursuing the mandated reduction. I am verifying the renewal-benchmarking memory because it most directly supports this action; memories on incumbent stability and multi-year volume pricing support continuity, while the low-cost-vendor memory is treated as leverage rather than a reason to switch under constrained capacity.
